Symptoms

Microsoft Outlook shows "Disconnected," "Trying to connect...," or "Need Password" in the status bar. Emails are not sending or receiving. Calendar and contact sync has stopped working.

Cause

Outlook connectivity issues are typically caused by incorrect Exchange server settings, expired or changed password, Outlook profile corruption, cached credentials conflict, or Exchange server maintenance/outage.

Resolution

  1. Check Outlook connection status: hold Ctrl and right-click the Outlook system tray icon, select "Connection Status."
  2. Test Exchange connectivity: run the Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer at https://testconnectivity.microsoft.com.
  3. Clear cached credentials: Control Panel > Credential Manager > remove Exchange/Outlook entries.
  4. Repair the Outlook profile: Control Panel > Mail > Email Accounts > Repair.
  5. Create a new Outlook profile if repair fails: Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add.

Workaround

Access email via Outlook Web App (OWA) at https://mail.company.com while troubleshooting the desktop client.

Verification

  1. Confirm Outlook status bar shows "Connected to Microsoft Exchange."
  2. Send a test email to yourself and verify it is received within 1 minute.
  3. Open Calendar and verify recent appointments are visible and synced.
